tonight.headline: The schedule complaint is finally dead: this run lands nine hours before Chem's waiver deadline. And the answer it arrives with is that nothing on the waiver list is worth claiming.
body: Two briefs in a row complained that this task fires six hours after Chem settles its claims. That complaint is now obsolete. Claims clear at 07:00 UTC - 01:00 Mexico City tonight - and you are reading this at 16:00 Mexico City. The window is open for about nine hours and this is the last brief before it shuts.

Having finally arrived in time to use it, I am telling you not to. Everything clearing tonight in Chem is a quarterback you just dropped, a receiver who ran 96.3% of his routes for zero targets, or a defence you are already better than. Claims are free here - priority resets weekly - but the claim is not the price. The drop is, and you only have one seat that is not freshly churned.
Your lineup is optimal on this snapshot: 126.20 projected, and the optimiser returns the same nine names you already have starting. That is re-derived, not carried.

The one thing that changed for the better today: McLaurin keeps your flex for a real reason now instead of on 0.6 projected points. Jalen Coker was limited at Carolina's Wednesday practice after being in a walking boot earlier in the week. That is the tiebreaker the last two briefs did not have.

case.label: The bad news about your own flex, first
case.body: Terry McLaurin was finally researchable this run and the news is not good. RotoWire on 13 September: two catches on four targets for 14 yards against Philadelphia in Week 1, while Stefon Diggs commanded nine targets and rookie Antonio Williams matched McLaurin's four. Jayden Daniels is throwing, and the target distribution in that offence is an open question rather than a settled hierarchy with McLaurin on top. He is still your flex, but he is holding it because Coker is in a boot, not because he earned it.

case.label: Why he still starts anyway
case.body: Washington travel to Dallas, who RotoWire note gave up the most passing yards in the league last season, and DraftSharks' Week 2 board has the Cowboys 16th of 32 - the softest draw among the three receivers competing for that flex. Coker is limited with an ankle and was booted on Monday; Brian Thomas Jr. is limited with a shoulder. Of the three, McLaurin is the only one who practised without a designation this week.

case.label: What decides the game
case.body: Panda Attack start five of their nine in two stadiums. Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams and George Pickens are all Cowboys hosting Washington; Davante Adams and Harrison Mevis are both Rams hosting the Giants. Two results move 56% of their lineup. That is a high-variance opponent in both directions, and on a 1.4-point projected gap it means the 51% is real noise rather than a lean.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker practises in full Thursday or Friday and carries no designation - then he is the better flex on matchup and the McLaurin hold flips. Also falsified if Washington's Thursday report adds McLaurin, or if Diggs's nine-target game turns out to be the shape of that offence rather than one script.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Both players lock Sunday 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Mack Hollins
doFirst.subtitle: Pitts cannot reach your lineup in this league at any price. Hollins can, he is free, and he inherits a 90-target hole.

case.label: Why Pitts is the drop and not a bench asset
case.body: Chem's flex is slot 3, RB/WR only. You have exactly one tight-end slot and Isaiah Likely is in it. Pitts's 11.3 projected points are not benched, they are structurally unreachable - his effective projection to you is zero unless Likely is hurt. STRATEGY section 9 says it outright: a second startable tight end has real value in IPADE and none in Chem, do not carry one. Yesterday's brief identified this and then did not act on it.

case.label: Disagreeing with the market on the record, as required
case.body: Pitts is 93.9% rostered and I am telling you to drop him. The market is right about Pitts and wrong about your league: almost every ESPN league flexes tight ends, so 93.9% of managers can start him and you cannot. This is not a read on Pitts the player. If Chem ever changes slot 3 to RB/WR/TE, this card reverses the same day.

case.label: Why Hollins, with the role fact attached
case.body: A.J. Brown is on injured reserve. FantasyPros' Week 2 waiver column names Hollins as the beneficiary specifically: elevated role after the Brown injury, four targets drawn after Brown went down, with red-zone access. That is a vacated role with a name on it - STRATEGY section 4's second-strongest add signal - and he is a free agent at 4.3% rostered, so he costs no claim and no priority. New England host Pittsburgh, 13th of 32 on DraftSharks' board.

case.label: The counter-argument from this morning, and where it is half right
case.body: The 13:05 brief kept Pitts on a specific reason worth answering: Likely plays Monday night, the last game of your week, so if he is ruled out you learn too late to replace him. That is right about claims and wrong about this wire. Mark Andrews is a FREE AGENT here at 82.0% rostered - no claim, no waiting period, addable the moment news breaks - and behind him sit Hockenson at 62.7%, Hunter Henry at 51.9%, Juwan Johnson at 53.5% and Pat Freiermuth, all free. Where the morning brief IS right: Andrews plays Sunday at 11:00 and Likely plays Monday at 18:15, so Andrews only covers you for news that arrives before Sunday. If Likely is ruled out on Monday itself, your only same-night option is Terrance Ferguson of the Rams, free at 22.0% rostered and projected 6.0. That is the actual exposure this card creates: one game, one bad Monday, about five points.

case.label: The churn rule, checked rather than assumed
case.body: Three of your bench seats changed hands this morning at 07:14 - Coker in for Stafford, the Ravens defence in for Jacksonville, Tyler Loop in for Boswell - and section 3 closes those for seven days. Likely arrived 13 September and Brian Thomas Jr. on 12 September. Pitts appears nowhere in the 53-row activity log, which reaches back to 12 September, so his is the only seat on the roster not recently churned. It is also the only one that cannot score.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Isaiah Likely appears on a Giants injury report before Sunday - then Pitts is your only tight end and this card is void until Andrews or another free agent is in the seat. Also falsified if Chem changes slot 3 to RB/WR/TE, which makes Pitts startable and reverses this the same day; or if beat reporting this week names DeMario Douglas or Romeo Doubs rather than Mack Hollins as the man absorbing A.J. Brown's targets, which would change the incoming player without changing the outgoing one.

whatWentWrong.title: The complaint that this schedule cannot reach a waiver run was true twice and is wrong now - and nobody noticed the 16:00 run already fixes it.
whatWentWrong.lead: Two consecutive briefs filed the same structural grievance: a 07:00 Mexico City task lands at 13:00 UTC, six hours after Chem settles claims at 07:00 UTC. Both were right about the morning run and both missed that a second run fires at 16:00 Mexico City, which is 22:00 UTC - nine hours BEFORE the next claims.

case.label: The arithmetic, redone
case.body: Chem claims clear at 07:00 UTC Thursday, confirmed from the clearsAt field on every waiver row in this snapshot, not from memory. That is 01:00 Thursday Mexico City. This run generated at 22:15 UTC Wednesday. The gap is eight hours and forty-five minutes, on the correct side. The morning brief is the one that cannot reach a waiver run; this one always could.

case.label: What the error cost
case.body: Nothing this week, because the answer tonight is 'claim nothing'. But it was filed as an unfixable structural defect in two briefs and written into the cannotSee section as a permanent limit, which is how a solved problem gets protected from being solved. The afternoon run is the waiver run. That is what it is for.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If Chem's waiver processing time moves off 07:00 UTC - the clearsAt field is the check, and it is read live every run - or if the 16:00 Mexico City task is rescheduled. Either would need this rewritten.

whatWentWrong.title: Kyle Pitts was correctly diagnosed this morning and then left on the roster anyway.
whatWentWrong.lead: The 13:05 brief worked out that Pitts is structurally unreachable in Chem, wrote it up as a finding, and produced no card. A finding that does not become an action is a note to yourself.

case.label: What was already known at 13:05
case.body: That Chem's flex excludes tight ends, that Likely holds the only TE slot, and that Pitts's 11.3 projected points are therefore worth zero. All three were in this morning's whatWentWrong section. The doFirst list was empty at the same time.

case.label: Why it did not become a card, and why that reasoning was thin
case.body: Presumably the churn rule - but the churn rule closes seats that recently changed hands, and Pitts's seat has not changed hands in the entire 53-row activity log. The rule that was actually being applied was 'do not manufacture cards', which is a good rule pointed at the wrong target: declining to act on a structural defect you have already proved is not restraint.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The activity log turns out to understate Pitts's tenure in a way that puts his arrival inside seven days - the log only reaches 12 September, so I can show he did not arrive in the last four days, not that he did not arrive in the last seven. If he arrived on 10 or 11 September, the seat is closed until Friday and this card waits.

worthALook.name: Mark Andrews
worthALook.lead: Still the loudest ownership anomaly on this wire, and today it stops being a pickup argument and becomes an insurance argument.

case.label: What is real
case.body: 82.0% rostered nationally and sitting free in a ten-team league is the strongest single wire signal STRATEGY section 4 recognises - it usually means a manager blundered. FantasyPros' Week 2 column has him at 4 catches for 49 yards on 7 true targets, describing him as a full-time option after injuries around him, while being lukewarm on his ceiling.

case.label: Why he is a note and not a card
case.body: He is a tight end, and the card above is about why you cannot use a second tight end in Chem. Adding Andrews to replace Pitts would fix nothing - you would still have one unusable TE, just a better one. He matters for a different reason: he is the proof that if Isaiah Likely gets hurt, an 82%-rostered starting tight end is available to you for free, immediately, with no claim and no waiting period. That is what makes dropping Pitts safe rather than reckless - with one honest limit. Andrews plays Sunday at 11:00 and Likely plays Monday at 18:15, so Andrews covers you only for news that lands before Sunday. For a Monday-morning ruling your only same-night tight end is Terrance Ferguson of the Rams, free at 22.0% and projected 6.0.

case.label: When to act
case.body: The moment Isaiah Likely appears on a Giants injury report or is ruled out. Then Andrews is a same-day free-agent add, not a claim. Also act if another Chem manager takes him, which would remove your insurance and is worth knowing about even though you cannot prevent it.

worthALook.name: Braelon Allen
worthALook.lead: New this run. The second name on FantasyPros' Week 2 list with an actual role attached, and the fallback if Hollins is gone before you act.

case.label: The role fact
case.body: FantasyPros' Week 2 waiver column lists him as a red-zone scoring threat complementing Breece Hall in a meaningful role - not a handcuff waiting for an injury, but a back with defined short-yardage work now. That is the opposite of the Tuten profile you are already unhappy with.

case.label: Why he is below Hollins
case.body: Your three flex-eligible receivers are all carrying something - McLaurin's target share collapsed to 4, Coker is limited with an ankle, Brian Thomas Jr. is limited with a shoulder - while your running back room is the healthy part of the roster. The need is a receiver, so the receiver goes first. Green Bay's defence is 7th of 32 this week, which is a hard Jets draw anyway.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Breece Hall appearing on a Jets injury report, which would turn a complementary red-zone back into a lead back overnight. Or Mack Hollins being rostered before you act, which promotes Allen to the card.

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: The trap the last two briefs called without checking. I checked it. It is worse than they thought, and tonight is the last chance to not make the mistake.

case.label: The fact that settles it
case.body: FantasyPros' Week 2 waiver column puts Addison at 96.3% route participation and ZERO targets in Week 1. He was on the field for effectively every snap and was not thrown to once. That is not a slow start or a bad script - it is a receiver being ignored, and route share without targets is the single most misleading number on a waiver wire.

case.label: Why the context makes it worse, not better
case.body: This happened in a game Minnesota won 39-22 as a comeback, in which Carson Wentz threw three touchdowns - two to Justin Jefferson and one to T.J. Hockenson. The offence produced plenty. Addison got none of it. And the quarterback who ignored him is the quarterback starting again on Sunday, with Kyler Murray still in concussion protocol and no return timeline.

case.label: What it would cost you
case.body: The claim itself is free - Chem priority resets weekly. The cost is the roster spot, and your only uncommitted seat is the Pitts seat, which is going to a receiver with an actual vacated role. Spending it on a 75.6%-rostered name because the number looks high is precisely the ownership-signal trap in reverse.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A Thursday or Friday report placing Jefferson in doubt, which would redistribute the targets Addison is not currently getting. Or beat reporting this week explaining the zero as scheme rather than preference. Absent either, let him clear.

doNotChase.sources: FantasyPros · Football Nation USA · league wire clearsAt

doNotChase.name: 49ers D/ST
doNotChase.lead: Biggest ownership move on the entire Chem wire for the second run running, and the answer is still no - but the margin is thinner than yesterday claimed.

case.label: Why the market is moving
case.body: Yahoo's Week 2 streaming column names San Francisco as a top stream explicitly, on the grounds that Miami looked like 'one of the worst units in the NFL after one week'. DraftSharks have the 49ers 3rd of 32. The move is rational and the defence is genuinely good this week.

case.label: Why you still hold
case.body: DraftSharks have your Ravens 4th of 32 against a New Orleans side that allowed 31 points to Detroit in Week 1. One ranking place, and ESPN price the 49ers 7.8 against Baltimore's 7.6 - a 0.2 gap, well under STRATEGY section 10's one-point floor. You also claimed this defence at 07:14 this morning, so the seat is closed under section 3 for seven days.

case.label: The honest wrinkle
case.body: The same 49ers defence is a problem for you in the other direction: De'Von Achane runs into it on Sunday. You are not chasing it, but you should know the board rates that matchup as bad for your own back and that is priced into his POOR tile above.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore appearing on a bye, or New Orleans being revealed as a better offence than Week 1 suggested. Neither applies. Revisit next week as a normal stream comparison, not as a chase.

candidates.note: Mack Hollins, WR NE, free at 4.3% rostered. Promoted to the doFirst card above; listed here so the reasoning survives if you do not act today. A.J. Brown is on injured reserve and FantasyPros' Week 2 column names Hollins as the man whose role was elevated, with four targets drawn after Brown went down and red-zone access. The low ownership is the opportunity, not the warning - it means nobody in a ten-team league has had to think about New England's receiver room yet. He is the add because your receiver group is the injured part of the roster, not the running backs.

Romeo Doubs, WR NE, free at 59.8% rostered. DOWNGRADED AGAIN and probably finished. The last two briefs carried him as the A.J. Brown beneficiary. FantasyPros' Week 2 column describes his Week 1 as a terrible game - zero catches on three targets, plus an interception charged against him - and names Mack Hollins rather than Doubs as the player whose role actually rose. Two runs pointed at the right hole and the wrong man. He stays listed only so a future run does not rediscover him and call him new.

Pat Freiermuth, TE PIT, free at 19.2% rostered, +4.56 this week. Recorded, not recommended, and for a structural reason rather than a performance one. FantasyPros have him 5-for-5 on targets in Week 1 with goal-line involvement, which is a genuine role signal. He is also a tight end, and the whole point of today's card is that Chem's flex will not take one. He is relevant to you only as Likely insurance, where Mark Andrews at 82% rostered is the better free version of the same idea.

cannotSee.label: Dropping Pitts leaves one uncovered scenario and I want it named
cannotSee.body: If Isaiah Likely is ruled out on Monday itself - after the Sunday slate has played - every free tight end on this wire except Terrance Ferguson has already played, and you would start Ferguson at 6.0 projected instead of Pitts at 11.3. That is roughly a five-point downside on a scenario that requires Likely to be healthy all week and then ruled out on game day. I judge that worth trading for a flex-eligible receiver you can actually start in the other 95% of outcomes, but it is a real cost and this brief should not pretend the insurance argument was worthless.

cannotSee.label: The Pitts drop rests on an activity log that only reaches 12 September
cannotSee.body: The churn rule asks whether a seat changed hands in the last seven days. The league file gives 53 activity rows going back to 12 September - four days. I can prove Pitts did not arrive in the last four days, not the last seven. If he arrived on the 10th or 11th the seat is technically closed until Friday, in which case this is a Friday card rather than a today card.

cannotSee.label: Matchup grades are one board, read in one direction, before any real defensive sample
cannotSee.body: Every tile derives from DraftSharks' Week 2 2026 defence board, which ranks defences as fantasy units - sacks and turnovers - rather than as coverage against a specific position. Two weeks into a season there is no per-position defensive sample to use instead. The runbook is explicit that these are judgement, not data, especially before week 4.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending claims are invisible and tonight is when they resolve

Matthew Stafford, Jordan Addison, Makai Lemon, the Patriots, Chargers and Jaguars defences, Chris Boswell and Jonah Coleman all clear at 07:00 UTC tonight. Someone may be claiming Mack Hollins as a free agent while you read this, and I would have no way to know.

cannotSee.body: It is a photograph taken at 21:52 UTC on Wednesday 16 September. Waivers clear in about nine hours, Josh Allen plays tomorrow, Thursday and Friday practice reports land before the Sunday slate, and Isaiah Likely does not play until Monday night. The Coker ankle read in particular has two more practice days to move.
